variants.name: A-four-pillars
variants.direction: COMPOSITION A: closest to the supplied reference. Wordmark small at upper left and badge A upper right. Centered huge two-line headline in the upper third, supporting sentence centered below on maximum two lines, then the understated existing-tools note. In the middle-lower area use FOUR white feature cards in one horizontal row. Each card has its exact heading and short description in the upper half, then an art-directed interface crop in the lower half, clipped elegantly into the rounded panel. Card heights around 360px at 2048px width. Keep 28px gaps and generous inner padding. The illustrations are supporting, not dominant. Reserve a separate quiet footer strip with all three jury answers. Refined Swiss editorial balance, no arrows connecting the four cards. Large blank breathing space between hero and cards.
variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Create ONE premium 16:9 English pitch-slide IMAGE for Physical Impact, approximately 2048x1152. Use the supplied image only as a STYLE REFERENCE: its generous whitespace, huge clean typography, warm off-white background, dark evergreen ink, mint accents and white softly rounded feature panels with cropped interface details. Do not copy its voice-call product or wording. This is a Physical Impact commercial pitch slide. Flat slide, no browser chrome, no device, no photographed screen. Precise, restrained, elegant, extremely readable. The audience should understand the offer in five seconds.

STYLE: background #F7F8F7, white panels, near-black evergreen #082A20, mint #48BF95, fine pale gray borders, Inter-like sans serif. No glow, 3D, gradients behind the whole page, stock photos, robot icons, giant orbit diagrams or decorative arrows everywhere. Use hierarchy and space. A restrained mint highlight on a few headline words is welcome. Main heading must remain high contrast. Feature illustrations are clean small UI crops with real short labels rather than many gray loading bars. No dense miniature dashboard.

SAME COPY AND CONTENT FOR ALL THREE VARIANTS:
Wordmark "Physical Impact" with one tiny mint mark.
Large main headline: "Adapt as fast as your market changes."
Supporting sentence: "An agent that knows your business, turns market intelligence into a coordinated response and executes the actions you approve."
Quiet secondary note: "Works in your workspace and through your existing tools."
Do NOT use headless as the product title or primary value. That complementary ability is already conveyed by the secondary tools note.

Four product pillars:
1. "Knows your business"
   "Your stock, suppliers, customers and commitments."
2. "Sees what matters"
   "Market changes, risks and opportunities."
3. "Coordinates the response"
   "One plan across procurement, operations, sales and finance."
4. "Acts with approval"
   "Execute in your tools. Verify results. Retain decisions."

Product UI illustration labels can use only short purposeful copy: first pillar "Stock", "Suppliers", "Commitments"; second "Supply disruption", "New demand"; third "Procurement", "Operations", "Sales", "Finance"; fourth a clear button "Review & approve", and the small continuation "Execute → Verify → Remember". These are illustrative product concepts, not actual operation receipts. Do not show a completed real purchase, named connector or an invented measured outcome. Full vision is company knowledge + market intelligence + coordinated plan + approved action + verification + retained decisions.

At the bottom, maintain a sparse three-column text strip, not more cards:
"WHO IT'S FOR"
"Teams that buy, make, move and sell physical goods. First: timber, steel and construction materials."
"WHY NOW"
"Late information can stop production, deliveries and projects."
"FIRST USERS"
"Targeted industry outreach. Start with one supply workflow, then expand across sites."

All these supplied text blocks must be present and correctly spelled, but do not repeat copy elsewhere. Let whitespace occupy a large part of the composition. The footer is subordinate but plainly readable; don't turn it into tiny footnotes. No extra paragraph, disclaimer, status banner, benchmark, synthetic/test/demo wording, architecture, sponsor logos, pricing, traction, time-saving metric or fabricated testimonial. Sell the clear product vision with calm confidence. Keep native-sized margins and visually balanced type. Label this concept with its single variant letter in a tiny pale mint badge at top right; that is an exploration label only.

variants.name: B-one-ready-response
variants.direction: COMPOSITION B: centered bold two-line headline in the upper third with restrained mint highlight, same brand/header/copy/tools note. Instead of four floating feature cards, show ONE large clean white shared product canvas in the middle, with the subtle title 'Your next response is ready'. Inside that canvas, four connected but distinct editorial columns carry the exact four pillar headings, descriptions and their clean cropped UI illustrations. Thin gray vertical dividers, lots of padding, no heavy dark banner. The fourth column has the prominent evergreen Review & approve button, and verification/retention visibly continues below it. This should feel like a single prepared company response spanning teams. Keep a quiet sparse three-column jury footer separated from the canvas by generous whitespace. Badge B top right. Preserve the reference's off-white, mint, evergreen and typography, avoid the old blue dashboard aesthetic.

variants.name: C-editorial-bento
variants.direction: COMPOSITION C: an airy asymmetrical editorial slide. Small wordmark upper left, badge C upper right. Hero occupies the left 42%: very large left-aligned headline on three clean lines, supporting sentence below, and quiet existing-tools note. Right 52% contains FOUR white softly rounded feature cards in a balanced 2x2 grid. Each contains its exact pillar heading and description plus one minimal purposeful UI crop, with ample whitespace rather than large icons. Keep the card copy comfortably readable, no crowded mini dashboards. The first two cards establish knowledge and market intelligence; the lower two show coordination and approved action with verification/retention. Across the bottom, outside the cards, the same sparse three-column jury footer. Same colors, fonts, content, 16:9 output and polish as A/B, while the split layout gives a genuinely different composition.
